To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dietary supplementation of PP and vitamin E to broiler chickens fed OTA contaminated diets improved the antioxidant status and quality of the meat, and PP supplementation improved the water holding of meat.
dietary supplementation with PP improved meat quality, antioxidant status and reduced the oxidative stress of broiler chickens exposed to OTA.
supplementation of diets contaminated with ochatoxin A with polyphenol product and vitamin E improved the antioxidant status of broiler chickens and improved water holding capacity of the meat.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of dietary supplementation with antioxidants (PP and vitamin E) on the antioxidant status, meat quality and fatty acid composition in the breast muscles of broiler chickens exposed to stress.

the influence of dietary supplementation with PP on the antioxidant status of broiler chickens, as well as the effects of dietary supplementation with vitamin on the oxidative status of broiler exposed to stress induced by OTA.
the effect of polyphenol product and vitamin E supplementation on antioxidant capacity, meat quality and lipid composition in broiler chickens fed OTA contaminated diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of PP and vitamin E as dietary supplements can be recommended to improve the antioxidant status of broiler chickens exposed to OTA.
dietary supplementation with PP and vitamin can be used for the mitigation of OTA-induced oxidative stress and the improvement of meat quality in broiler chickens.
dietary supplementation with vitamin A and/or PP is an effective tool to improve antioxidant status and meat parameters of broiler chicken fed diets naturally contaminated by OTA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary supplementation with vitamin and PP enhanced the total antioxidant status of broiler chickens exposed to oxidative stress caused by a high dose of OTA.

the dietary supplementation with vitamin and polyphenols E improved the antioxidant status in chickens exposed to stress caused by OTA, however, this effect was not translated into an improvement of the carcass traits.
PP is an efficient tool to improve meat quality and antioxidant status of broiler chickens exposed to stress induced by OTA in diets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PP can be used as an alternative to vitamin E in broiler chickens exposed to stress.
the use of polyphenols as a feed additive for broiler chickens can be recommended to reduce the adverse effects of OTA on meat quality.
dietary supplementation with vitamin C and/or E may be an effective tool to improve the antioxidant status of broiler chickens exposed to stress and contaminated with mycotoxins.
